questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'acting in the client's best interest'?

options.A: Maximizing the advisor's commission while meeting minimum requirements
options.B: Putting the client's interests ahead of the advisor's own interests
options.C: Selling products that are suitable regardless of cost
options.D: Meeting regulatory requirements without exceeding them

questions.stem: Confidentiality in the advisor-client relationship means that client information:

options.A: Can be shared with colleagues for educational purposes
options.B: Must never be disclosed under any circumstances
options.C: Should only be disclosed with client consent or when legally required
options.D: Can be used for marketing purposes if anonymized

questions.stem: A conflict of interest arises when:

options.A: An advisor earns commission on products sold
options.B: An advisor's personal interests may interfere with acting in the client's best interest
options.C: A client disagrees with the advisor's recommendation
options.D: An advisor works for multiple employers

questions.stem: When an advisor discovers they have made an error that negatively affects a client, they should:

options.A: Wait to see if the client notices the error
options.B: Immediately disclose the error to the client and take corrective action
options.C: Correct the error without informing the client
options.D: Consult with compliance before taking any action

questions.stem: The 'know your client' (KYC) rule primarily requires advisors to:

options.A: Verify the client's identity to prevent money laundering
options.B: Understand the client's financial situation, needs, and risk tolerance
options.C: Maintain regular contact with all clients
options.D: Document all client communications

questions.stem: Suitability in retirement planning means:

options.A: Recommending only low-risk investments to retirees
options.B: Ensuring recommendations align with the client's circumstances and objectives
options.C: Selecting the products with the highest returns
options.D: Choosing investments that match the advisor's risk tolerance

questions.stem: An advisor who holds themselves out as a specialist in retirement planning:

options.A: Must have at least 10 years of experience
options.B: Should possess appropriate credentials and maintain competence in the area
options.C: Can use any title they choose
options.D: Is not subject to additional ethical obligations

questions.stem: When providing retirement income projections, an advisor should:

options.A: Use optimistic assumptions to motivate clients
options.B: Use conservative, realistic assumptions and clearly disclose them
options.C: Guarantee minimum returns based on historical averages
options.D: Avoid making any projections to limit liability

questions.stem: An advisor receives a referral fee from an insurance company for recommending their products. The advisor:

options.A: Can accept the fee without disclosure if it doesn't affect recommendations
options.B: Must disclose the referral arrangement to clients
options.C: Cannot accept referral fees under any circumstances
options.D: Only needs to disclose if the client specifically asks

questions.stem: When a client makes a decision that the advisor believes is not in their best interest, the advisor should:

options.A: Refuse to implement the client's decision
options.B: Document the discussion and implement the decision if it's legal and within the client's rights
options.C: Implement the decision without discussion to respect the client's autonomy
options.D: Report the client to regulatory authorities

questions.stem: Professional indemnity insurance (errors and omissions insurance) is important because it:

options.A: Eliminates the need for careful documentation
options.B: Protects advisors from regulatory investigations
options.C: Provides financial protection if a client suffers losses due to advisor errors
options.D: Allows advisors to take greater risks with client investments

questions.stem: The primary purpose of the CIFP Code of Ethics is to:

options.A: Increase the profitability of financial planning practices
options.B: Protect the public and maintain the profession's integrity
options.C: Minimize legal liability for advisors
options.D: Create barriers to entry for new advisors

questions.stem: An advisor discovers that a colleague is engaging in unethical behavior. The advisor should:

options.A: Ignore it if it doesn't directly affect their own clients
options.B: Report the behavior to the appropriate authorities or regulatory bodies
options.C: Confront the colleague privately but take no further action
options.D: Wait until multiple complaints accumulate before reporting

questions.stem: Continuing education requirements for retirement professionals primarily serve to:

options.A: Generate revenue for professional organizations
options.B: Ensure advisors maintain current knowledge and competence
options.C: Create networking opportunities
options.D: Justify higher fees to clients

questions.stem: When communicating with clients, an advisor should:

options.A: Use technical jargon to demonstrate expertise
options.B: Communicate in clear language appropriate to the client's level of understanding
options.C: Focus only on positive aspects to maintain client confidence
options.D: Avoid discussing risks to prevent client anxiety

questions.stem: The 'prudent investor rule' requires retirement advisors to:

options.A: Invest only in guaranteed products for clients over age 65
options.B: Exercise the care, skill, and diligence that a prudent person would use
options.C: Achieve returns that exceed market benchmarks
options.D: Avoid all investments with any element of risk

questions.stem: A life annuity provides income payments that:

options.A: Continue for a specified number of years regardless of survival
options.B: Continue for the lifetime of the annuitant
options.C: Can be withdrawn as a lump sum at any time
options.D: Are guaranteed by the federal government

questions.stem: The primary advantage of a term-certain annuity over a life annuity is:

options.A: Higher monthly payments
options.B: Guaranteed payment period regardless of survival
options.C: Better inflation protection
options.D: Lower tax liability

questions.stem: A Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC) is best described as:

options.A: A deposit product offering guaranteed interest for a fixed term
options.B: An insurance product providing lifetime income
options.C: An equity investment with principal protection
options.D: A government bond issued by the Bank of Canada

questions.stem: Segregated funds differ from mutual funds primarily in that segregated funds:

options.A: Always have higher returns
options.B: Provide maturity and death benefit guarantees
options.C: Have no management fees
options.D: Cannot be held in registered accounts

questions.stem: The Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) insures eligible deposits up to:

options.A: $50,000 per depositor per member institution
options.B: $100,000 per depositor per member institution
options.C: $250,000 per depositor per member institution
options.D: $500,000 per depositor per member institution

questions.stem: A prescribed annuity offers tax advantages because:

options.A: Payments are entirely tax-free
options.B: The taxable portion is level throughout the annuity's life
options.C: It can be held in an RRSP
options.D: Capital gains treatment applies to all payments

questions.stem: A variable annuity differs from a fixed annuity in that:

options.A: Payments are not guaranteed and fluctuate based on investment performance
options.B: It cannot be held in registered plans
options.C: It has no death benefit
options.D: It is not offered by insurance companies

questions.stem: Bonds are subject to interest rate risk, meaning that:

options.A: Bond issuers may default on interest payments
options.B: Bond prices fall when interest rates rise
options.C: Interest payments may be taxed at higher rates
options.D: Bonds cannot be sold before maturity

questions.stem: The primary purpose of holding fixed income investments in a retirement portfolio is to:

options.A: Maximize long-term capital growth
options.B: Provide stability and regular income
options.C: Achieve tax-free returns
options.D: Protect against inflation

questions.stem: Real Return Bonds (RRBs) are designed to protect investors against:

options.A: Stock market volatility
options.B: Credit risk
options.C: Inflation risk
options.D: Currency risk

questions.stem: A laddered bond portfolio involves:

options.A: Buying bonds with staggered maturity dates
options.B: Investing equal amounts in stocks and bonds
options.C: Reinvesting all interest payments
options.D: Selling bonds before maturity to realize gains

questions.stem: The cash surrender value of a permanent life insurance policy:

options.A: Equals the death benefit
options.B: Is the amount available if the policy is cancelled
options.C: Is guaranteed to equal premiums paid
options.D: Cannot be accessed during the policyholder's lifetime

questions.stem: A reverse mortgage allows homeowners aged 55+ to:

options.A: Borrow against home equity without selling the home
options.B: Refinance their existing mortgage at a lower rate
options.C: Receive government grants for home renovations
options.D: Transfer their home to beneficiaries tax-free

questions.stem: Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWPs) from investment accounts:

options.A: Guarantee a specific income for life
options.B: Provide regular withdrawals that may deplete capital
options.C: Are only available within RRSPs
options.D: Must withdraw the same dollar amount each period

questions.stem: The primary advantage of a joint and survivor annuity is:

options.A: Higher initial payment amounts
options.B: Payments continue to the surviving spouse after the first death
options.C: Better tax treatment of payments
options.D: Full capital is returned to the estate
